title: Longest Non-decreasing Subarray From Two Arrays
spaceBreakdown:
- int variables dp0, dp1, ndp0, ndp1, ans, i: constant → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vectors nums1, nums2
approach: At each index i, nums3[i] is either nums1[i] or nums2[i]. The longest non-decreasing run ending at i depends only on which value was chosen at i and which was chosen at i−1, so we track two DP states: the best run length ending with nums1[i] and with nums2[i]. For each state we try extending from either previous state whenever the non-decreasing condition holds, defaulting to 1. We keep only the previous index's two values, giving O(1) auxiliary space.
hints: When extending a non-decreasing run to position i, what do you need to know about position i−1 to decide whether nums1[i] or nums2[i] can continue the run? The arrays have up to 10^5 elements.
Dynamic programming with two states per index: dp0 = best run ending with nums1[i], dp1 = best run ending with nums2[i]. In Example 2 at i=2, nums2[2]=3 ≥ nums1[1]=3, so dp1 = dp0_prev + 1 = 3.

**Single element** - n=1, no previous index to compare with
`nums1 = [5], nums2 = [3]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: starting the loop at i=0 and accessing nums1[i-1] → out-of-bounds read

**All equal values** - every adjacent pair is non-decreasing only with `<=`
`nums1 = [2,2,2], nums2 = [2,2,2]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: using `>` instead of `>=` in the comparison → returns 1

**Cross-array optimal** - the best run must switch from nums1 to nums2 mid-stream
`nums1 = [5,1], nums2 = [3,4]` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: tracking only the state ending with nums1[i] → returns 1

**Stale state carryover** - a long run ends, then a shorter valid run continues
`nums1 = [1,2,1,1], nums2 = [1,2,1,1]` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: initializing ndp0 = dp0 instead of 1 when no transition applies → returns 3

followUps.q: What if you are given k arrays instead of 2?
followUps.a: Maintain k states per index. For each state j, dp[i][j] = 1 + max over all k' where array_j[i] >= array_k'[i-1] of dp[i-1][k']. Keep only the previous row. TC: O(n·k²), SC: O(k).

followUps.q: What if you want the longest non-decreasing subsequence (not subarray) of nums3?
followUps.a: The contiguity constraint disappears, so the two-state-per-index approach no longer works. Compress all 2n candidate values, then use a segment tree or Fenwick tree to query the best run ending at any value ≤ nums_j[i]. TC: O(n log n), SC: O(n).

followUps.q: What if the arrays arrive as a stream and you can only store O(1) elements?
followUps.a: The current solution already processes one index at a time and keeps only the previous two state values plus the current two. Feed pairs (nums1[i], nums2[i]) one at a time and update in place. TC: O(n), SC: O(1).
